flip_era: No 1990s care-ratio break detectable. Consistent series (care = parks+libs+health; cage = police, city lines only): 1992 = 0.56 (Census year, full coverage), 1998 = 0.36, 1999 = 0.33, 2025 anchor = 0.06. Direction is DOWN not up: through Renaissance-II (1994-99) police grew $57.5M->$69.8M while parks fell $19.6M->$10.6M and library fell out of the city's visible lines. The apparent 1992->1998 'break' down partly reflects annual-survey coverage loss (library + welfare lines go dark), but the police-side growth is real.
confidence: Medium — 1992 data is Census-of-Governments high-quality, full coverage. 1998/99 annual-survey partial. Modern anchor only has 2025-actual for police/fire/parks lines, and no library line city-side.
falsifier: If a future find puts city-wide 1980s Pittsburgh budget with same code-level breakdown (Census of Governments 1982 or 1987 city files), and 1980s care/cage matches or exceeds 1998-99 values, the "care ratio break during Renaissance-II" hypothesis is dead. Best candidates to break the deadlock: Census of Governments 1982 & 1987 city files, or Pittsburgh PA Annual Financial Report 1980s (city controller, archived).
